main_text.p: quodque reipublicæ membrum pro aris & focis stare tenetur, & bona, parentes, liberos , conjugem , patriam tueri, ejusque securitatem redemptam cupere, etiam cum sui ipsius internecione. HocInit.in-ftir. Ex-cuf. Fu-tor. ipsum passim collaudat jus civile. Quienim pro patriâ moritur, in perpetuum per gloriam vivere creditur. Qui su-[?]pervivit,honoribusac præmiis,l.35. D. de Relig. & sumpt. Gloss.in l,velut. 2.D. de iustit. & quæ meritus est afficiendus. Quinimo non tantum licí-tum, aut liberè relictum, pro patria sic decertare, sed etiam jur. & insi occasio suadeat, omnino necessarium censebitur.

Quo nomine historiis proditum exemplum mulieris La-l. fallaci-cenae, quae cum accepisset filium ignavo erga patriam fuisse ter. Cod.animo, domum reversum occidit, ejusque sepulchro hosce de Abo-versus inscribi curavit: Hunc lit.timidum mater Damatrion ipsa Valer.peremit[?]. Max. libr.

page.notes: Page is cut off after "pro"; the lower part is not in this image. Doubtful readings: "su-" in "Qui su-pervivit" (the first letter looks like f or s, marked [?]); "giof." in the right-margin note (marked as printed, the word may be "Gloss." or "Relig."). The note at "l.35." runs over several lines in the margin and is given in full as far as it is legible. The top right note line is cut at the scan edge; its first word reads as "juris.&" or "jur. &" and is marked uncertain in the note text. The word "peremit" is uncertain; a sign may stand over the e. Show-through and the faint marks at the far right are not printed text. The catchword "Nec" stands at the right below the last line.
